# What hosted CI actually checks, and what it does not.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. .github/workflows/build.yml produces a row of green
# checks on every commit to main, and a reader who sees them reasonably
# concludes the commit was fully verified. For a long time it was not: the
# test suite did not run hosted at all, and nothing said so in a form a
# machine could check, so the gap was invisible to exactly the person the
# checks exist to inform — someone who does not trust this machine and is
# reading the commit on GitHub. The suite is hosted now (see the `tests`
# row), which is precisely why this file must keep saying what each check
# does and does not cover: the failure mode was never a missing job, it was
# a green whose meaning nobody had written down.
#
# This file is the declared coverage, and tools/lint/check_verification_coverage.sh
# holds it to the workflow. It cannot drift: every item claiming to be hosted
# must name a job key that really exists in build.yml, and every job in build.yml
# must be claimed by some item. Adding a job without declaring what it verifies
# fails lint; claiming an item is hosted when its job was renamed or deleted
# fails lint.
#
# THE FIVE ITEMS ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE HERE. The gate hard-codes the required item
# list (gcc, clang, lint, tests, fuzz-replay) in its own file, so the gap cannot
# be closed by deleting a row. That two files must agree is the point — the same
# discipline check_promotion_receipt_chain.sh prong 6 documents, added there
# after a mutation reworded a message and a same-file self-test still passed.
#
# Format — five `|`-separated fields, one item per line:
#
#   item | hosted | job_key | display_name | attested_by
#
#   item          short name of the verification item.
#   hosted        exactly `yes` or `no`. Nothing else parses.
#   job_key       the YAML key under `jobs:` in build.yml when hosted=yes;
#                 exactly `-` when hosted=no. NOT the display name: matrix job
#                 names are templated (`compile-check (${{ matrix.cc }})`) and
#                 never appear literally in the file, so a display-name match
#                 would be checking a string that is not there.
#   display_name  the check name a reader sees on GitHub, for humans only.
#   attested_by   where the verdict comes from when hosted=no. Must be
#                 non-empty; `-` when hosted=yes. An item that is not hosted and
#                 does not say who vouches for it is an unverified claim.
#
# CONFIRMATION STATUS — read this before quoting any row as verified.
#
# The gcc, clang, lint, fuzz-replay and compile-all-tus rows were each confirmed
# against a real check-run attached to commit df752afce on origin/main (run
# 30509201499, all five success).
#
# The `tests` row is hosted and is now CONFIRMED hosted-green. Its first
# hosted run was RED, and this file tracked that honestly (see the ARCHIVED
# paragraph below, kept verbatim for the record). See the confirmation
# paragraph below for the run id and verdict line that closed it.
# Its current job forces `--no-cache` and admits only one semantic cold verdict:
# nonzero groups executed, zero cache hits/failures/environment-unobserved legs,
# and `groups_ran + groups_gated == groups_total`. The verifier's mutation
# self-test specifically proves that a cached zero-run headline is rejected.
#
# The `arena` row is hosted. It is the only job that runs the three commands
# the README gives a stranger, from a clean checkout, with no vendored-
# dependency cache and no restored build tree. It re-derives the Arena roots
# pinned in tools/dev/arena_demo.sh — roots that were produced on the
# maintainer's host — on a machine nobody here controls, so it is also the
# cross-machine half of the reproducibility claim docs/ARENA.md makes. It
# does NOT verify consensus, the node, or anything the other rows cover.
#
# CONFIRMATION STATUS OF THE FIX (2026-07-30). `make lint` (128 gates) and
# `make test-parallel -j"$(nproc)"` — the exact commands build.yml's `lint`
# and `tests` jobs run — both pass clean on commit 722e25a14 on this host,
# gated the same way the workflow gates them: `ALL TESTS PASSED` present,
# `SOME TESTS FAILED` absent. The suite's own verdict line: groups_total=846
# groups_ran=842 groups_gated=4 (params-heavy, same as the first hosted run)
# groups_failed=0 self_skips=25. Each of the four fixed test groups was also
# re-run 8-15 times in isolation with zero flakes.
#
# HOSTED CONFIRMATION (2026-08-17) — this closes the pending status above.
# Run 32001633676, commit 0d154f6c3 on origin/main. All six jobs success,
# `tests` among them. The suite's own verdict line from that run's log,
# quoted rather than inferred:
#
#   SUITE VERDICT mode=cold groups_total=939 groups_ran=930 groups_cached=0
#   groups_gated=9 groups_failed=0 self_skips=26 toolkey=c84ebf8a37e1
#
# Two further hosted-only defects were found and fixed between the local
# confirmation above and this hosted green, both of the same class the
# `tests` job exists to catch — a green that depended on the maintainer
# host's ambient state:
#
#  7. test_dev_platform attributed a cancellation to the wrong resident
#     process under cold/concurrent conditions (fixed in 93933f260).
#
#  8. test_test_group_selector's Make admission probe ran
#     `make -n t-fast-exact ONLY=api`, which exits 2 on a COLD checkout and
#     0 on a warm one. Root cause is general and was not in the test:
#     `$(file >...)` is a make FUNCTION, evaluated when a recipe line is
#     EXPANDED, and make expands every recipe line under -n in order to
#     print it. Every response-file recipe therefore WROTE its file during a
#     dry run and died when the epoch directory did not exist yet, because
#     the mkdir that creates it lives in a recipe -n only prints. `make -n`
#     on any test goal was broken on every cold checkout. Fixed by guarding
#     all nine sites on ZCL_MAKE_NO_EXEC (Makefile). The same test also
#     buffered the whole dry run into 8 MiB against a claimed ~2 MB worst
#     case; a cold clone emits 12.2 MB and the assertion it needs is in the
#     tail truncation would have dropped, so it now captures a bounded head
#     and a bounded tail and discards the middle.
#
# WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, one paragraph per fix, each independently
# root-caused by reading the real code path and reproducing the mechanism
# locally — no guessing:
#
#  1. test_chain_integrity_failed_condition read the operator's REAL default
#     datadir. remedy_chain_integrity_failed() resolves GetDataDir()
#     unconditionally, and on UNRECOVERABLE it can open
#     blocks/blk00000.dat at genesis. Without SetDataDir() the test silently
#     read whichever real datadir happened to be there — the live node's, on
#     the maintainer host. Fixed by pinning it to a fresh hermetic tmp dir.
#
#  2. test_proof_validate_stage (joinsplit_sig case) and test_pv_lookahead
#     (real-verifier differential) need the real Sapling prover, driven by
#     the ~770MB param files that are not in the repo and are not fetched by
#     CI. Fixed by making both legs self-skip loudly (the `SKIP (` sentinel
#     test_parallel already counts) when the params are absent, instead of
#     failing — every other case in both files already uses an injected test
#     verifier and needed no params.
#
#  3. test_block_status_event_restart_proof's boundary-height assertion
#     asserted the event log and the stage cursor could never be found out of
#     sync at the cursor height. They are two INDEPENDENTLY durable stores,
#     written in that order by rp_process_one (mirroring the real
#     body_persist_stage / script_validate_stage call sites), so a kill
#     landing between the last event write and the cursor advance can
#     legitimately leave the projection one write ahead of the cursor — not
#     corruption, since every field is a deterministic function of height and
#     reprocessing re-derives identical bytes. The assertion fired on that
#     benign race. Fixed by asserting the real invariant instead: the
#     boundary height, if present at all, is never CORRUPTED.
#
#  4. test_zcode_policy identified its own just-planted event file by keeping
#     the last 64-hex-char filename readdir() returned that didn't start with
#     'a'/'b' — order-dependent on ext4's per-filesystem htree hash seed, and
#     wrong roughly 1-in-8 of the time regardless (a real SHA3-256 id can
#     legitimately start with 'a' or 'b'). Fixed with a before/after exact-name
#     set difference.
#
#  5. test_make_lint_gates_shard_08's systemd-memory-budget self-test read the
#     ambient host's /proc/meminfo instead of the pinned deploy-target value
#     the lint job already uses — coincidentally correct on the maintainer
#     host, wrong on a small hosted runner. Fixed by pinning the same value
#     the lint job pins.
#
#  6. NEW, found this session while proving the above four fixes: running the
#     FULL suite (not per-group --only runs) surfaced a fifth, previously
#     undetected failure in test_make_lint_gates_shard_07's
#     check-fuzz-artifact-ledger self-test — not one of the original six.
#     tools/lint/check_fuzz_artifact_replay.sh decides whether to trust git
#     enumeration by checking only that `git rev-parse --git-dir` succeeds,
#     on the assumption that it fails inside the lint-gate self-test's git-less
#     `cp -al` sandbox. It does not fail: git's upward search for `.git`
#     climbs PAST the git-less sandbox (which lives under
#     .claude/worktrees/<name>.lint_sb_<pid>/) into the real outer
#     repository's .git a few levels up, so "git available" reports true —
#     just pointed at the wrong tree. Since .claude/worktrees/ is itself
#     gitignored there, both enumeration passes silently returned zero
#     artifacts instead of erroring, tripping the gate's own "at least 20
#     found" sanity check. Confirmed by instrumenting the script inside a
#     live failing sandbox run: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` printed the
#     outer repo's root while the script's own computed $ROOT was the sandbox
#     path underneath it. Fixed by comparing --show-toplevel against $ROOT
#     and only trusting git when they match.
#
# ARCHIVED — the original hosted-red paragraph, kept verbatim for the record.
#
#   First hosted run: 30516674384, commit be432065d, 2026-07-30. The other
#   five jobs succeeded. `tests` FAILED in 10m52s — not a timeout; the job
#   limit is 120 minutes, so a hosted runner carries this suite comfortably.
#   Its own verdict line: groups_total=846 groups_ran=842 groups_gated=4
#   groups_failed=6 self_skips=25, 308.2s wall, 4 workers.
#
#   Six groups failed, in three classes. This is what the job was built to
#   find.
#
#    1. READS THE DEFAULT DATADIR — a real defect, not a runner quirk.
#       test_chain_integrity_failed_condition never calls SetDataDir, so it
#       resolves to ~/.zclassic-c23 and the runner logged
#       `cannot open /home/runner/.zclassic-c23/blocks/blk00000.dat`. On the
#       maintainer host that path is the LIVE NODE and is populated, so the
#       test has been passing by reading the live node's block files:
#       silently weakened, and touching a datadir no test may touch. An
#       independent machine proved it; the maintainer host structurally
#       cannot.
#
#    2. REQUIRES THE SAPLING PARAMETERS — test_proof_validate_stage
#       (joinsplit_sig case) and test_pv_lookahead. `read_file failed for
#       sapling-spend.params`. These need a ~770 MB artifact that is not in
#       the repository and is not fetched by CI, and unlike the
#       params_missing case in the same file — which passes, because it is
#       written for absent params — they do not self-skip.
#
#    3. UNDIAGNOSED, possibly real ordering bugs.
#       test_block_status_event_restart_proof (2 assertions: `boundary
#       height never falsely reported complete`, `fixture fully folded`),
#       test_zcode_policy (`corrupt wires skipped and counted, facts
#       intact`), and test_make_lint_gates_shard_08 (`P1-3 systemd memory
#       budget: baseline and selftest pass`, baseline_rc != 0). No error is
#       printed for the first two; they may be assumptions about scheduling
#       or readdir order that only hold on the maintainer host. Nothing here
#       has been root-caused yet and none of it is claimed to be
#       environmental.
#
#   The permitted resolutions are unchanged: fix the coupling (classes 1 and
#   3), or declare a smaller hosted scope IN THIS FILE naming exactly what is
#   excluded and why (class 2, where the blocker is an artifact nobody
#   ships). Class 2 may self-skip only if the skip is loud and counted — a
#   skip that coasts silently has already cost this project a week of
#   hollow green. The dishonest resolutions, ruled out: trimming the corpus
#   until it passes, gating on a narrow tail/grep instead of the full
#   output, or editing this paragraph to assert a confirmation that did not
#   happen.

gcc|yes|compile-check|compile-check (gcc)|-
clang|yes|compile-check|compile-check (clang)|-
lint|yes|lint|lint (make lint)|-
fuzz-replay|yes|fuzz-replay|fuzz-replay (saved findings)|-
compile-all-tus|yes|build|build (cached dependencies)|-
tests|yes|tests|tests (make test-parallel)|-
arena|yes|arena|arena (make arena-demo)|-
